title: Dimension-based attention modulates early visual processing
description: Continuous 64-channel scalp EEG from 12 observers performing a visual dimension-based attention (cue) task, originally reported by Gramann, Töllner and Müller (2010). The recordings, 56-66 minutes each, include ICA decomposition weights and expert-annotated independent component labels. The dataset was later used to study automatic multi-class labeling of ICA components and is known as the "Cue" dataset.
methods_description: 64 scalp EEG channels were recorded referenced to Cz and re-referenced offline to linked mastoids. ICA was performed with the infomax algorithm in Brain Vision Analyzer. Twelve right-handed observers (age 21-25) performed a visual task. Expert labels of independent components are provided along with ICA weights and sphere matrices. Data were provided by Laura Frølich and, with permission from Klaus Gramann, converted to BIDS format by Austin J. Brockmeier and Carlos H. Mendoza-Cardenas.
